I've planned round 460 as a fix of round 459, which failed C's check. The decision in `b-next.json` is **CONTINUE**.

**What round 459 found.** The new black entrance screen fails when a browser extension inserts something into the page before it loads. React then redraws the whole page, the cover's style element is replaced, and the entrance animation never plays. The previous version (HEAD) still plays it in that case. A found this and stopped, and C confirmed it independently. It is a Medium bug, and the gap was in my round-459 plan. Gate 459 was skipped, and the round-459 changes stay in the store uncommitted.

**The fix (v2c).**
- The entrance state now lives on `window`, which survives the redraw, instead of on the style element.
- The early skip listeners (Esc, Tab, click) now remove themselves after 1250 ms.
- After a redraw the black screen stays on until the animation takes over. It never re-blackens a page that is already showing.
- It stays inside the same five files as round 459, and `app/root.tsx` is unchanged.

**Proof before handing it to A** (production builds in real Chromium; I edited nothing in the store):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Animation plays after the forced redraw | HEAD 3/3, round-459 version 0/3, v2c 3/3 |
| Redraw actually happened | confirmed in every `inject`/`delayinject` row on v2c |
| Black first frame | every row |
| Slow page load plus redraw | no animation (by design) and no re-blackening |
| Hydration warnings on a separate dev server | 0 in 6/6 runs |
| Full timing matrix | 78 rows across both viewports and normal/4× CPU |
| Entrance tests | 41/41 pass |
| Tests for the changed code | 11 files / 206 tests pass |
| Type check / lint | clean / 207 warnings, unchanged |
| Deliberately broken versions of the fix | all 27 make the tests fail |

tech-lead's first review asked for one change: a stale state could re-blacken an already visible page. I made it, and the second review approved the exact patch.

**The other two round-459 failures were measurement problems, now ruled:**
- The logo/tagline minimums still apply at normal CPU speed. At 4× CPU slowdown they are recorded only, because the 1.9 s cap squeezes the logo there; my own runs also fell below the old minimum. Saba's 1.45 s minimum still holds at both speeds.
- Skip speed is now measured from the actual key or click, which removes the test tool's own delay. My maximum was 128 ms; the new limits are 200 ms at normal CPU and 400 ms at 4×.

**The advisor was available and used twice.** The second call caught seven problems, all fixed. The most important: C's redraw checks could have passed without the redraw ever happening, so they now require proof that it did. Findings I had closed on my own evidence are open again until C confirms them.

**Bookkeeping:**
- backlog v452 records the round-459 result (D-29z1626) and the round-460 dispatch (D-29z1627), and feature-status shows SABA-B-13 as ბაგია → მუშავდება.
- The round-459 task is archived in `tasks/round-459.md`.
- There is one new non-blocking question for Saba (SABA-Q-ENTRANCE-BACKGROUND-TAB, default: keep the current behaviour).
- The regression round is due from 2026-11-13, so round 461 will be regression if it is planned on or after that date.
- Firefox and Safari can't be checked in the cloud; that stays a Tech Lead manual check due by RETRO 465.

The full plan is in `b-round-459.md`.
